description: Frame-latency wait: the flip-model swap chain is created with DXGI_SWAP_CHAIN_FLAG_FRAME_LATENCY_WAITABLE_OBJECT, IDXGISwapChain2::SetMaximumFrameLatency(1), and R_SyncGpu, right after the lost-device check and its first clock read (so the wait counts against com_maxfps), waits on the waitable object once for each present the render thread made since the last wait. The wait for present p returns once present p-1 is on screen: one frame stays queued while the next frame's mouse is read (IN_Frame runs right after R_SyncGpu in every client state). Pairing by counted presents means frames that weren't presented are never waited for. Each wait times out after two refresh periods (50 ms to 1 s) and is alertable. A timed-out wait, or a present the window procedure made (fullscreen switch), makes the next frame take every pending signal instead of counting. A lost device's new swap chain gets a new object and the counts start again. Falls back to no wait without IDXGISwapChain2 (flip model without the flag, then the original swap chain, when the system refuses it). Otherwise R_SyncGpu is the original, compared call for call with the Store build. Keys and mouse buttons after the wait: P0009.

com_maxfps goes up to 1000 (the original's maximum is 100, B0024); default 85 and minimum 0 (uncapped) unchanged. Com_Frame still turns a cap into whole-millisecond frames (1000/k fps) and never takes less than 1 ms. Every other registration is the original's.

The view kick from firing on a fixed 5 ms grid (B0063): for the cgame's kick arrays the real state advances only in whole 5 ms steps of the original, the rest of the frame time carried; the cgame sees that state advanced to the frame time by one more original step, recomputed every frame. A change made elsewhere (a shot, a spawn) restarts the grid from that state, so the kick after a shot is the same function of time at any frame rate, bit for bit the original's at 200 fps at every multiple of 5 ms. The kicked angles go into the usercmd, so the server sees the same kick at any frame rate. Other callers (bots) get the original.

The viewmodel's recoil on a fixed 5 ms grid of the cgame's time (B0064): whole original 5 ms steps, plus one step of the rest for what is shown, recomputed every frame; keyed on weaponState_t::time, so a second call at the same time doesn't advance it; a shot or the time going back restarts the grid. Bit for bit the original at 200 fps at every multiple of 5 ms.

Usercmds of a fixed 5 ms (200 Hz) whatever the frame rate (B0057-B0061): a command at lastCmdTime += 5 while it is due by cl.serverTime, at most 20 a frame, leftover carried, re-anchored after a jump of more than 500 ms. Movement (Pmove runs once per command, rounding the velocity each step) is then the same at every frame rate: jump peak 39.06 units, the original's at com_maxfps 100; commands never repeat a time, never overflow a packet. Keys measured over the span the frame's commands cover, buttons latched until a command reads them, extra buttons in the first command only; mouse, keyboard and gamepad turning update the view angles every rendered frame. Each frame a temporary command at cl.serverTime with the frame's angles (cl_viewCmd) is built for the view, never stored or sent. The default-command mode keeps one command per frame. Key timing is exact to within one command at a press or release. docs/fps.md 6.5.
